Subject: Billing shaping & savings opportunities — post-discovery recap

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the 45min call this morning. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move to a scoped pilot: summary, confirmed pain points, numbers you shared, and immediate next steps.

Summary (what we heard)
- Budget/gating: team has a hard monthly inference budget of ~$18k for the first pilot phase.
- Volume: ~1.2M generation requests / month, average 450 tokens per request (user prompt + assistant).
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for 1k concurrent users in peak region (US-East).
- Data posture: customer data cannot leave US, needs audit logs and basic KMS integration.

Token economics (back-of-envelope from call)
- Current provider: approx $0.00012 per token => est $54k/mo (unacceptable).
- Opportunity areas we discussed: batching, prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts, model quantization, and model routing to cheaper variant for low-sensitivity flows.
- Projected savings (very conservative): batching + cache => 35–50% token/time reduction; quantization & routing => additional 10–20% unit-cost reduction. Full-stack pilot TCO will refine these.

Proposed pilot scope (what I recommend)
- 8-week POC focused on chat Q&A flows with two routes: (1) high-fidelity route (p95 <= 220ms), (2) economical route (slower but cheaper).
- Deliverables: cost model (per-token and per-session), dashboard access (latency and cost by route), security checklist for your audit.
- Success criteria: < $18k/month projected at scale with p95 latency <= 250ms on primary route; 30%+ unit cost reduction for non-critical flows.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Priya/Ravi: confirm the monthly token/request numbers above or send last 30d export for exacts.
2) Redwood: we’ll share the attached high-level levers estimate (redwood_token_levers_estimate.xlsx) and a draft pilot scope by EOD tomorrow.
3) If procurement/finance are involved, loop them in now — we’ll need contract/PO timelines for a June kickoff.

Attachments: redwood_token_levers_estimate.xlsx (savings scenarios), pilot-scope-draft.docx (initial POC scope).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a one-page cost snapshot once we have the last-30d numbers.

Priya/Jordan —

Quick technical note to address Priya’s ask about caching/no-cache scenarios and expected hit rates. High level assumptions below — happy to slot a 30min deep dive with Ravi/your infra team.

Assumptions based on the average chat flow you described:
- 450 tokens/request; 60% of sessions have repeated system prompts / templated prompts that benefit from KV/prefix caching.
- We expect KV cache TTL of 24 hours for identical prompts in typical support-style workflows.

No-KV baseline (what you’d see if you don’t integrate caching):
- Per-token cost = model unit price + infra overhead; batching alone (if you accept up to 50ms queuing) gives ~18–22% improvement in tokens/throughput.

With KV/prefix caching enabled:
- Effective token reduction: 30–45% on top of batching (depending on prompt repetitiveness). For your 1.2M requests, conservative estimate => ~36% fewer generated tokens.

Quantization and model routing:
- 4-bit quantized variants for non-Safety-critical route: ~12–18% unit-cost improvement vs float16 on modern runtimes.
- Routing policy: classify requests at entry (sensitivity flag) and steer to economical variant where acceptable. Latency delta small for cached flows.

Combined conservative projection (batching + KV + quantization): ~45% unit-cost reduction vs current baseline. End-to-end pilot will produce a calibrated number; we’ll publish the strain-tested projection to the shared Drive link.

I uploaded a short calc to the project Drive and added a default pilot SLO matrix. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cLedgerWorks-cost-model

If you want, Ben and I can put together a three-scenario spreadsheet (Cold/Hybrid/Full) with explicit POI/ROI lines for procurement.
